title: How far is a drawn angle from the asked angle?
description: In a second game, one team announces an angle and a player of the other team draws it without a protractor. The drawing is measured, and the smaller number is taken from the bigger number to find the miss. Keeko thinks a wider drawing costs nothing.
teaching_notes: One idea: the miss is the bigger number minus the smaller number, for a drawing that is too small and for a drawing that is too big. Watch for students who think a drawing wider than the asked angle is not a miss.

source: Same two teams, new rules. Team 1 announces to all an angle
video_script.why: The child learns to compare a drawn angle with the asked angle, and to find how far the drawing missed the target by taking the smaller number from the bigger one.
video_script.substitution: The second game of the book: an asked angle of thirty four degrees and a drawing that measures twenty five degrees.
video_script.anchor: a board with an angle drawn by hand, and a protractor laid over the angle to read it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks overshooting costs nothing, because the angle is bigger than asked. Missing the target on either side gives a gap, so a wide angle is no safe choice and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Team two gets nine as its penalty
maths_rules: asked angle = 34 degrees, measured drawing = 25 degrees
the gap between the drawing and the asked angle = the bigger number minus the smaller number = 34 - 25 = 9 degrees
a drawing that is too small and a drawing that is too big both leave a gap
in the book the team that draws gets as many points as the gap, and the lowest total over five turns wins
check: counting up from 25 to 34 takes 9 steps
video_script.design: One idea: the miss between a drawn angle and the asked angle is the smaller number taken from the bigger number. The drawn angle stays on the board all video, and the two numbers sit side by side on a number line.
open_questions: The book calls the gap the score in points. The video calls it a penalty, and says that the lowest total wins.
